name: CA-46
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 10-point Democratic lean plus favorable environment
Correa's incumbency and $2.5M cash advantage over Pan's $6K
No general-election polling, leaving fundamentals-based uncertainty
model.rationale: Lou Correa holds a seat that leans Democratic by double digits, has outraised David Pan by roughly 15-to-1 with a huge cash-on-hand edge, and markets price his reelection at 96%. With no polls or expert ratings to move the picture, the fundamentals-based margin of about 20 points stands essentially unchanged.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Correa would be the first sign of movement in an otherwise quiet race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lou Correa seeks another term in a Southern California district that voted about ten points Democratic at the presidential level. He advanced to the general election as the incumbent and enters November with a large financial edge: roughly $2.5 million on hand against about $6,000 for Republican David Pan, who raised under $100,000. Outside spending has been minimal and one-sided in Correa's favor.

Prediction markets give Correa about a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public general-election polling, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing, all pointing to a comfortable Correa victory with modest residual uncertainty.
